name: Private browsing detection
plain: Infers whether the browser is in a private or incognito window.
meaning: Sites use it for metered paywalls and fraud scoring. Browsers keep closing the leaks (quota size, filesystem API, IndexedDB errors), so any method has a short life.

web.api: navigator.storage.estimate() quota, IndexedDB open errors, FileSystem API, timing

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can often tell if you are in a private window, until browsers close the gaps
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Check storage size and errors that differ in private mode
Block a metered paywall trick or add a fraud score
Ask you to leave the private window
cannot: See what you browse in the private window
Work for long; browsers keep fixing these tells
Be certain; each method can fail
Stop the private window from working

story.what_it_is: Guesses whether you are in a private or incognito window.

marketing.name: Incognito mode in Chrome
marketing.pitch: Chrome says Incognito does not save your browsing history on the device, but sites can still see your visit.

story.for_you: You never see the check. You may notice a site that refuses to open a free article in private mode, or asks you to sign in. Your private window looks like any other, but the site may treat it differently.
story.for_makers: Publishers use it to enforce free article limits that would reset in a private window. Fraud teams treat private browsing as a mild risk signal. Browsers keep closing the clues, so each method works only a short time.

use_cases.example: A newspaper with a few free articles a month blocks private windows, since they would reset the counter.
A payments fraud system adds risk when a new account is created in private mode.
A retail site cannot keep your cart across visits in private mode and shows a note.
A browser games portal tells you progress will be lost when you close the private window.
A bank notes that a login came from a private window and may ask for an extra code.
An ad vendor treats private browsers as users who opted out of tracking.
An online exam provider blocks private windows to stop hidden helper tools.

risks: May block people who value privacy

technical_bounds: Cannot see history or cookies of the normal window

linkedin.how: Incognito or private mode detected. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
